memo.verdict: PARK. Direction neutral. Conviction medium. Overall grade [D]. The memo publishes as the written record of why Viewforth is not spending Early-Stage Assessment hours on Salvatore Ferragamo (SFER-IT) at EUR 9.605, and holds the name on the luxury goods watchlist with a quarterly review cadence rather than excluding it. The park is not a judgement that the turnaround is fake. It is a judgement that the operating repair is real and the entry point has closed. The memo's own one-line case: Viewforth would have wanted this stock on 15-May-26 at EUR 6.61; at EUR 9.605 it is being asked to underwrite a turnaround at 45.0x with 7% of the sell-side rating it Buy. Four named re-entry triggers. (1) A permanent chief executive appointed with proven luxury leather goods scale-up credentials. (2) Leather goods organic growth above 5% for two consecutive quarters. (3) Quarterly store sales density reaching EUR 15k per square metre against EUR 12k now. (4) A trading multiple back inside the bottom half of its own ten-year range, or a consensus target price above rather than 26% below the market price. Anti-trigger confirming the park: full-year FY26 organic revenue growth below 2%, or gross margin contracting below 68% on renewed promotional activity.
case: The case for parking runs in four steps, and the memo makes them in this order.

Step one: the base fails, not the change. Element E1 Required Attribute 2 (Robust base) grades [F], and it is the single Required Attribute that drives the recommendation. External headwinds are present on every axis and several are worse here than for peers: Americas exposure of 40% against an industry average near 20%, a currency mismatch where the euro is about 85% of cost of goods sold and 70% of capital expenditure while the dollar is 37% of revenue and only 5% of production cost, and a hedging horizon of up to 24 months against a 12-month standard at Burberry, Moncler, LVMH, Kering, Richemont and Prada. The base is under-invested on every measure available: marketing at about 8.0% of sales, design spend of EUR 25.08m, vertical integration of about 1%, capital expenditure cut to EUR 46m in FY25, density of EUR 12k per square metre, 344 inventory days and 42% to 43% staff turnover. The delivery record is broken: the 2022 plan targeted doubling revenue to EUR 2.2bn by FY26 against FY25 actual of EUR 976.53m, the 18.5% operating margin ambition has been reset to a consensus near 4.5% by FY28, and the company changed chief executives four times in ten years.

Step two: the mispricing has closed even though the change-from-current has not. The change-from-current is genuinely large, with no permanent chief executive, no permanent chief financial officer, a strategy reversal, two flagship closures and a wholesale exit all live. But the shares have moved from EUR 6.61 on 15-May-26 to EUR 9.605 on 14-Aug-26, the twelve-month return is 112.1%, the consensus target of EUR 7.15 sits 26% below the price, only 7% of the pool rates the shares Buy, and the price sits 19.1% above the 200-day average and 119% above the 52-week low. The multiple is 45.0x at an 82nd percentile of its own ten-year history, or 56.1x on the live price against the same file's forward earnings. Enterprise value to sales of 2.2x looks cheap against Hermes at 9.0x, Brunello Cucinelli at 4.5x, Moncler at 4.3x and LVMH at 3.2x, but those peers earn 16.8% to 41.1% operating margins against 4.5% here, so the sales multiple is a depressed-margin artefact and buying it assumes a margin normalisation management has promised and missed twice.
counter_case: The Risks family's own stage recommendation, quoted in the memo: "we recommend a hold and watch posture rather than progressing the idea immediately, matching Morgan Stanley's underweight stance", and "the investment is too risky for a concentrated long-only portfolio until brand heat shows sustained and positive momentum". The memo ADOPTS this recommendation. There is no conflict on the stage decision. It agrees that the cost-driven nature of the profit recovery, the EUR 12k per square metre density gap, the leather goods contraction and the leadership vacuum are all correctly identified and correctly weighted. It parks for a partly different reason: the Risks family parks on brand-heat deterioration, the memo parks on the entry point and case complexity.

Three disagreements with the Risks family's reasoning, recorded rather than suppressed. First, the false-friend verdict is overstated: the analysis-of-competing-hypotheses scores the false-friend profile with zero hard inconsistencies against nine for the turnaround profile and four for the collapse profile, but operating cash flow of positive EUR 70.60m against negative EUR 8.58m, and 150 basis points of gross margin gain on full-price mix and a deliberately shortened sale period, are inconsistent with a pure false friend, so on that evidence the zero looks like one or two rather than zero. Second, the downside targets look too low: Morgan Stanley models EUR 4.00 and Jefferies EUR 4.50 in the bear case, yet neither appears to weigh net cash excluding leases of EUR 124.54m against free cash flow of EUR 52.68m in a single half. Third, the price anchor is stale: the Risks family computes 56% to 61% downside from a EUR 10.25 trading price whereas the master-dashboard close on 14-Aug-26 is EUR 9.605, so its stated downside percentages are overstated by roughly six percentage points.
triggers: Trigger 1, governance. A permanent chief executive appointed with proven luxury leather goods scale-up credentials. This would resolve four of the nine change-from-current items into a single accountable owner and is the cleanest single re-rating trigger available. The search has run for over seventeen months without a candidate; Jefferies notes historical management tenure has averaged under three years over the last decade.

Trigger 2, product. Leather goods organic growth above 5% for two consecutive quarters, driven by direct-to-consumer handbag platform expansion beyond the Hug bag. This is the test that would move Element E8 Required Attribute 4 Core Question 9 off its [F] answer on mid-term business quality. Leather goods fell 0.7% organically in Q2-26 against consensus of plus 4.2%.

Trigger 3, productivity. Quarterly store sales density reaching EUR 15k per square metre, against EUR 12k now and a peer benchmark above EUR 24k. Density is the bottleneck: with operating costs guided flattish from here, every remaining leg of margin recovery depends on it.
Trigger 4, price. A trading multiple back inside the bottom half of its own ten-year range, or a consensus target price that sits above rather than 26% below the market price.

Anti-triggers confirming the park. Full-year FY26 organic revenue growth below 2%, or gross margin contracting below 68% on renewed promotional activity. The Risks family sets its own re-run trigger at any gross margin deterioration below 69%.

Watch items carried from the element work. Flagship reopening milestones, Beverly Hills late 4Q26 and New York 1Q27, as the cleanest test of execution against a published date. The July 2026 trading slowdown, disclosed voluntarily at the H1 print and attributed to softer United States demand, adverse weather and a shorter sale period, and whether it extends into Q3 and Q4. The United States tariff position, since a settled 20% rate would remove roughly 30% of operating profit without pricing offsets, with a Section 122 10% tariff live for up to 150 days and a reimbursement petition pending at the Court of International Trade. Italian workshop consolidation, specifically further conglomerate acquisitions of tier-one processing suppliers, as the leading indicator of supply foreclosure. Average unit retail and full-price sell-through across primary United States and Asian boutiques, named by the Business Foundations family as the early-warning signal.
